parsed.explanation: No documented traveler-facing criminalisation, facility ban, border/document targeting, detention or organised violence. Bathroom access is protected, hate-crime and anti-discrimination law covers gender identity, and reporting/complaints routes exist nationally with no regional legal variation. Residual risk is everyday friction and low, non-disaggregated hate-crime counts, plus unspecified acknowledged gaps and undocumented foreign-document/border practice, keeping the case below the near-perfect 0.95 anchor.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No reported refusal, secondary inspection, or rejection of foreign passports/X markers.
entry_documents.protection: Self-determination and X marker for residents, and bathroom/document protections as climate signals; no direct traveler document guarantee documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home passport; resident X-marker regime does not itself determine foreign-document acceptance.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No arrests, custody placement, searches, or detention practice targeting trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate-crime/anti-discrimination law and complaints mechanism indicate functioning institutional recourse, not a custody protocol.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document mismatch, if it occurred, would be subject to general law; no documented escalation pathway.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility exclusion documented. Sparse gay scene outside capital is not a facility ban.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Bathroom access protected nationally; legal protections described with no regional differences.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National protection applies uniformly despite scene concentration in capital.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No denial of emergency, routine, or medication care to trans visitors shown.
care_services.protection: Not documented as a traveler-facing care guarantee; resident legal protections are climate signals only.
care_services.interaction: Ward placement or medication import could arise in an emergency, but dossier gives no operative rule.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminal offence, cross-dressing, fraud, or threat-framing law documented; same-sex activity legal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 1996/2014 criminal-code protections, 2019 self-determination law, conversion-therapy ban; these signal trans-respecting institutions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Protective law and no documented hostile enforcement align, reducing outing consequences.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No traveler restrictions on trans minors or accompanying guardians shown.
minors_guardians.protection: Resident minors may change legal gender with parental consent, but that is not a visitor protection.
minors_guardians.interaction: A traveling minor follows guardian/home documents; no documented separate exposure or safeguard.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Potential hate crimes: 16 in 2023, 11 in 2024, 7 year-to-date; not disaggregated by target, small absolute counts, no trans-specific rate established.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National emergency guidance, victim reporting routes, hate-crime law covering gender identity, and equality complaints body.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Counts show some prejudice crime and a call for stronger legislation, but do not show police targeting or impunity for trans visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Acknowledged gaps in protection are unspecified; foreign-document, rural-attitude, and trans-specific incident data are thin/undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Official equality complaints committee and police hate-crime reporting routes are documented and national.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist on paper and institutionally; dossier does not show their outcomes in visitor cases.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: explicit equality/hate-crime coverage, protected facilities, complaint routes, residual friction. This case has no documented rural officer stop, so slightly higher, but traveler-specific remedy outcomes are less documented.
Higher: that anchor has brief detention and humiliating secondary screening despite respectful border training. No such traveler detention or screening is documented here.

Lower: 0.95 requires audited border practice, prompt corrections, and demonstrated respectful routine treatment. Here border/X-marker acceptance, care, and remedy outcomes for visitors are not documented, and gaps are acknowledged.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is nationally protective with no subnational hostile layer: protected bathroom access, gender-identity hate-crime coverage, and complaints routes operate uniformly. The main interactions are residual—home-passport acceptance and any emergency ward/care encounter are undocumented, and small non-disaggregated hate-crime counts prevent a trans-specific violence assessment. No universal-exposure measure, organised targeting, or state threat-framing is documented, so consequences after outing are primarily ordinary friction and discrimination risk with institutional recourse.
